key_decisions.decision: Renders wise-hearted as practical skill while retaining divine filling and spirit of wisdom, not reducing it to unaided craftsmanship.
Keeps six garment categories and repeated purpose; patterned leaves precise tashbets textile technique open.
Keeps mishpat as judgment connected to rulings and later Urim/Thummim, not merely decorative jewelry.
Keeps first three Hebrew stone positions with provisional traditional mineral equivalents; exact identifications noted as uncertain.
Preserves nofekh-sappir-yahalom order with provisional names; sapphire matches the earlier 24:10 terminology.
Keeps leshem-shevo-ahlama positions without pretending modern mineral equivalents are established.
Keeps final three stones, shoham consistent with shoulder stones and all gold settings; names remain provisional.
Retains named objects and repeated judgment/heart language; notes their unresolved form and procedure without inventing a divination mechanism.
Preserves head opening, woven reinforcement, armor comparison and no-tearing purpose; rare tahra identification qualified in note.
Keeps audible entry and exit requirement and real death warning rather than ornamental symbolism.
Preserves bearing guilt of sacred gifts and acceptance purpose without substituting personal sinlessness or moralizing priestly responsibility.
Keeps three garment tasks and distinguishes patterned weaving from embroidered sash while leaving exact weave uncertain.
Unfolds actions distinctly and translates fill-the-hand idiom as ordain with literal wording explained for later ritual connection.
Keeps both service contexts, guilt and death, hereditary obligation and explicitly male priestly participants.
